# 1. History

## 1.1 Early Foundations (1960s-1970s)

| Year | Contribution | Researchers |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| 1960 | Delta rule for linear networks | Widrow & Hoff |
| 1970 | Automatic differentiation (reverse mode) | Seppo Linnainmaa |
| 1974 | "Applying the backpropagation rule" (thesis, unpublished) | Paul Werbose |
| 1976 | Connectionist models and backpropagation | Art Bryson |

## 1.2 The Breakthrough (1986)

**Rumelhart, Hinton, & Williams** published *"Learning representations by back-propagating errors"* in Nature, demonstrating that multilayer networks could learn internal representations.

```python

# This was the key insight that unlocked deep learning
```

## 1.3 The Dark Age (1990s-2000s)

- Neural networks fell out of favor due to:
  - SVMs and kernel methods dominance
  - Vanishing gradient problem in deep networks
  - Limited computational resources

## 1.4 The Deep Learning Revolution (2012+)

| Year | Event | Impact |
|------|-------|--------|
| 2006 | Deep Belief Networks | Hinton shows greedy layer-wise pretraining |
| 2012 | AlexNet wins ImageNet | GPUs + Backprop = Deep CNNs |
| 2015 | ResNet (152 layers) | Skip connections solve vanishing gradients |
| 2017 | Transformer architecture | Backprop through attention |
